Stability Landscape Across a Stability Measure

Source: R/stability_landscape.R
landscape_surface.Rd

The cups of stability_landscape() drawn as a surface over a second axis: a per-sequence stability measure from sequence_metrics(), such as self-loop tendency or longitudinal entropy. At each value of the measure, sequences are weighted by a tricube kernel on their distance to that value over the k nearest (Cleveland 1979), and each state's cup depth, \(-\log(1 - P_{ii})\) (the log of its expected stay), is computed from their weighted pooled transitions. Moving along the axis goes from the most stable to the most volatile sequences.

Usage

landscape_surface(
  x,
  measure = "longitudinal_entropy",
  states = NULL,
  k = 30L,
  n_grid = 25L
)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_surface'
summary(object, ends = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_surface'
print(x, digits = 2, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_surface'
plot(x, max_stay = 50, theta = 10, phi = 30, ncol = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A transition network from build_network() (method "relative" or "frequency"), a grouped one, or a wide sequence data frame or matrix. For the print() and plot() methods: an object of class net_landscape_surface.

measure

Character vector of numeric sequence_metrics() columns, one surface each. Default "longitudinal_entropy".

states

Character vector naming every state once, in drawing order. Default: alphabetical.

k

Integer. Nearest sequences per slice. Default 30 (capped at the number of sequences).

n_grid

Integer. Slices between the 5th and 95th percentile of the measure. If these percentiles coincide for a nonconstant measure, its full range is used. Default 25.

object

A net_landscape_surface object (for summary()).

ends

Logical. In summary(): TRUE (default) compares the low and the high end of each measure; FALSE returns every slice.

...

Ignored.

digits

Integer. Decimal places in print(). Default 2.

max_stay

Numeric. In plot(): cups of states whose expected stay exceeds this many steps (including states never left in a slice) are drawn at the depth log(max_stay), a display floor only. Default 50.

theta, phi

Numeric. In plot(): viewing angles passed to persp().

ncol

Integer or NULL. In plot(): panels per row. Default: one row per network, one column per measure.

Value

An object of class "net_landscape_surface" holding the slices as one data frame (one row per network, measure, slice and state), with states, measure and k.

In summary(): with ends = TRUE, a data frame with one row per network, measure and state: group, measure, state, low_value, depth_at_low, high_value, depth_at_high; with ends = FALSE, every slice (group, measure, value, state, depth, dwell, effective_n).

In print(): x, invisibly.

In plot(): x, invisibly; draws one persp() surface per network and measure on a shared depth scale.

Details

Network input replays per-sequence weighting, concatenation and boundary markers. Concatenated sequences are the resampling units. With a covariate, its value must be constant within each concatenated unit. Scaled, thresholded or otherwise modified networks whose weights do not match their stored sequences are refused; pass the original sequences to estimate a new landscape. Observed shares count prepared positions without sequence weighting. Phase windows retain the full sequence's weight.

The measures are computed from the same sequences as the depths, so the cups of the most stable sequences are deep by construction (self-loop tendency in particular is closely tied to the stay probabilities). What the surface adds is which cup deepens as stability rises. A slice's effective_n (\((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\)) shows how many sequences it rests on. A state that does not occur in a slice has an NA depth and leaves a gap in the surface.

Errors

nestimate_not_markov, nestimate_bad_input (unknown, non-numeric or constant measure, bad states), nestimate_landscape_unestimable (fewer than five usable sequences). Warning nestimate_thin_slice when slices rest on fewer than five effective sequences.

References

Cleveland, W. S. (1979). Robust locally weighted regression and smoothing scatterplots. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 74, 829–836.

Kramers, H. A. (1940). Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions. Physica, 7, 284–304.

See also

stability_landscape, sequence_metrics

Examples

net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
surf <- landscape_surface(net, measure = "longitudinal_entropy",
  states = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"))
surf
#> Landscape surface: 3 states, 1 network x 1 measure, 30 nearest sequences per slice
#> 
#> Cup depth (log of the expected stay) at the low and the high end of each measure:
#>               measure      state  low depth_at_low high depth_at_high
#>  longitudinal_entropy Disengaged 0.11         1.95 0.96          0.57
#>  longitudinal_entropy    Average 0.11         1.42 0.96          0.57
#>  longitudinal_entropy     Active 0.11         3.03 0.96          0.54
#> 
#> Effective sequences per slice: network 13.3-25.7
# \donttest{
plot(surf)

# }
